IEA, ICCA and DECHEMA (2013). Technology Roadmap: Energy and GHG Reductions in the Chemical Industry via Catalytic Processes. International Energy Agency, Paris. Annexes published separately online (TechnologyRoadmapCatalyticProcessesAnnexes.pdf), not held.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 2). A roadmap with scenario results; the per-process SEC tables (Annex 4, Table 5) are in the separate online annexes, which are NOT held - obtaining them would give SEC and GHG per process for the top 18 chemicals. Main file (8 examples): catalytic naphtha cracking pilot 10-11 GJ/t HVC (Han 2002) vs BPT steam cracking 12 GJ/t HVC (p.21); HVC-production step energies printed as labels in Figure 12 (MTO 5, ethanol dehydration 2, naphtha cracking 12 GJ/t HVC); stoichiometric process CO2 of ammonia from gas (1 t/t) and coal (2 t/t). _measures: HPPO (35%) and catalytic cracking (10-20%). _other-values: upstream feedstock-production energies of Figure 12-13, biomass GHG savings, hydrogen-route energy penalties (relative values), DECHEMA scenario totals. Traps: (1) text p.26 says naphtha cracking needs 5 GJ/t HVC, but Figure 12 shows 5 as naphtha production and 12 as cracking (checked on the rendered figure); (2) p.24 gives process CO2 of 1 and 2 t "per t MeOH" where footnote 15 says per t ammonia; (3) Figure 15 GHG labels not extracted (stack order unclear); (4) energy carriers and heating-value basis are never stated.
